I now have a comprehensive picture of the tutors-sdk ecosystem. Here is my complete report.

---

## Tutors-SDK Course Folder Structure -- Comprehensive Breakdown

### 1. COURSE ROOT FILES (Required)

Every tutors course requires these files at the root:

**`course.md`** (REQUIRED) -- The course title and description. The first line (after optional frontmatter) is treated as the title (leading `#` is stripped). The second non-empty line becomes the summary. The full body is the course's "info" content.

```markdown
# My Course Title

A short description of the course.
```

**`course.png`** (or `.jpg`, `.jpeg`, `.gif`, `.svg`) -- The course card image. This is the visual thumbnail shown in course listings.

**`properties.yaml`** (OPTIONAL but standard) -- Course-level configuration. Key properties:

```yaml
credits: Author name or credits line
slack: https://slack-url
moodle: https://moodle-url
youtube: https://youtube-playlist-url
teams: https://teams-url
zoom: https://zoom-url
parent: course/parent-course-id
auth: 0                    # 0=public, 1+=requires auth
labStepsAutoNumber: false  # auto-number lab steps
llm: 2                     # LLM integration level
ignorepin: 4321            # PIN to reveal hidden topics
portfolio: false           # treat as portfolio of courses
private: 0                 # 1=private course
hideVideos: false
defaultPdfReader: adobe    # or "mozilla"
pdfOrientation: landscape  # or "portrait"
footer: "Footer text"

ignore:                    # list of topic folder IDs to hide
  - topic-10-hidden

companions:                # custom companion links
  piazza:
    link: https://piazza.com/
    title: Piazza Q & A for this course
    icon:
      type: academicons:piazza
      color: info

iconset:                   # custom icon overrides
  moodle:
    type: fa-solid:graduation-cap
    color: warning
```

**`calendar.yaml`** (OPTIONAL) -- Defines a week-by-week calendar overlay.

**`enrollment.yaml`** (OPTIONAL) -- Enrollment/access control data.

**`vercel.json`** (OPTIONAL) -- For Vercel deployment:
```json
{
  "version": 2,
  "buildCommand": "npx -y deno-bin@latest run -A jsr:@tutors/tutors",
  "outputDirectory": "json",
  "framework": null
}
```

---

### 2. LEARNING OBJECT TYPES -- The Complete Taxonomy

The system recognizes learning objects by **folder name prefix**. The `findLastMatchingString` function in `resource-builder.ts` scans each folder path segment from right to left, matching against these prefixes:

**Simple types** (leaf content):
- `note` -- Rich markdown note
- `archive` -- Downloadable zip file link
- `web` -- External web link
- `github` -- GitHub repository link
- `panelnote` -- Note displayed at topic level as a panel card
- `paneltalk` -- Talk displayed at topic level as a panel card
- `panelvideo` -- Video displayed at topic level as a panel card
- `podcast` -- Podcast episode embed
- `talk` -- Presentation/lecture (PDF slides)
- `book` -- (alias for `lab`) Multi-step lab
- `lab` -- Multi-step lab walkthrough
- `tutorial` -- Tutorial with optional PDF

**Composite types** (containers that hold other LOs):
- `unit` -- A named section within a topic (rendered inline)
- `side` -- A sidebar section within a topic (rendered in sidebar)
- `topic` -- A major course section (top-level card on course page)
- `course` -- The root (implicit, not a folder prefix)

**Sort order** when displayed (from `preOrder` map):
course(0), unit(1), side(2), topic(3), talk(4), tutorial(5), book/lab(6/7), note(8), web(9), github(10), archive(11), panelnote(12), paneltalk(13), panelvideo(14), podcast(15)

---

### 3. FOLDER STRUCTURE FOR EACH LEARNING OBJECT TYPE

#### TOPIC
The primary structural unit. Folder name must start with `topic`.

```
topic-01-typical/
  typical.md          # Title (first # line) + summary (second line)
  typical.png         # Card image (any image extension works)
  unit-1/             # Units inside
  unit-2/
```

Or with frontmatter for custom Iconify icon (instead of image):
```
topic-09-svg/
  topic.md            # Can use frontmatter for icon
  topic.png           # OR an image file (icon overrides image)
```

The `.md` file can use YAML frontmatter:
```markdown
---
icon:
  type: emojione:owl
  color: blue
order: 3              # explicit sort order
---
# Topic Title

Summary text here
```

#### UNIT
Groups content within a topic. Folder name starts with `unit`.

```
unit-1/
  main-lesson.md      # Unit title/description
  talk-1-intro/       # Talks inside
  talk-2-explore/
  book-a/             # Labs inside
```

The unit `.md` file is simple -- just the title:
```markdown
Main Lesson
```

#### SIDE (Sidebar Unit)
Like a unit but rendered in a sidebar. Folder name starts with `side`.

```
side-unit/
  topic-labs.md       # Side title
  book-a/             # Labs
  book-b/
  book-c/
```

#### TALK (Presentation/Lecture)
Folder name starts with `talk`. Requires:

```
talk-1-intro/
  introduction.md     # Title (first line) + summary
  introduction.pdf    # The PDF slides (required for rendering)
  introduction.png    # Card image
  videoid             # OPTIONAL: YouTube video ID
```

The `.md` content:
```markdown
Lecture 1

A short summary of the talk, no more than two sentences.
```

The `videoid` file (when present) contains just the YouTube ID:
```
x09E7b2ESE8
```

You can also add `?start=1370&1802` for start/end times.

Frontmatter for custom icons:
```markdown
---
icon:
  type: bi:filetype-pptx
  color: green
---
Hidden Lecture

This lecture should not appear in the wall
```

#### LAB / BOOK (Multi-step Walkthrough)
Folder name starts with `book` (internally mapped to type `lab`). This is the most complex type.

```
book-a/
  00.Lab-01.md        # Step 0 (title step - first # line becomes lab title)
  01.01.md            # Step 1
  02.02.md            # Step 2
  03.03.md            # Step 3
  ...
  07.Exercises.md     # Last step
  img/                # Images referenced in steps
    main.png          # Lab card image (MUST be named "main.xxx")
    01.png
    02.png
  archives/           # Optional downloadable archives
    archive.zip
  videoid             # OPTIONAL: associated video
```

Step naming convention: `NN.title.md` where:
- `NN` is a two-digit sort prefix (00, 01, 02...)
- The text between the first `.` and last `.` becomes the step's `shortTitle`
- The first `# Heading` inside the file becomes the step's full title
- Files are sorted alphabetically, so numeric prefixes control order

The `img/main.png` file is special -- it becomes the lab's card image.

#### NOTE
Folder name starts with `note`. Rich markdown content.

```
note-1/
  note.md             # Full markdown content (title from first # line)
  note.png            # Card image
  img/                # Images used in the note
    01.png
    02.png
  archives/           # Optional downloadable zip
    archive.zip
```

Notes support full markdown: images, code blocks with syntax highlighting, math notation (LaTeX), tables, embedded videos (`::video[src="..."]::`) and podcasts (`::podcast[src="..."]::`)

The `.md` file can have any name, but it must be the ONLY `.md` file in the folder (the system picks the first `.md` file found).

#### PANELNOTE
Identical structure to `note`, but folder starts with `panelnote`. Displayed as a panel card directly on the topic page rather than inside a unit.

```
panelnote/
  note.md
  note.png
  img/
    01.png
```

#### PANELTALK
Identical to `talk` but displayed as a panel card on the topic page.

```
paneltalk/
  talk.md
  talk.pdf
  talk.png
```

#### PANELVIDEO
Video panel displayed at topic level. Requires:

```
panelvideo-1/
  video-main.md       # Title/description
  videoid             # YouTube video ID (just the ID string)
```

The `videoid` file contains the YouTube ID:
```
x09E7b2ESE8
```

For HEAnet/VIMP video services:
```
heanet=MEDIA_ID
```
or
```
vimp=MEDIA_KEY
```

#### WEB (External Link)
Folder name starts with `web`. Links out to a URL.

```
web-1/
  tutors-web-site.md  # Title + summary
  tutors-web-site.png # Card image
  weburl              # File containing the URL (first line)
```

The `weburl` file is a plain text file with the URL on the first line:
```
https://tutors.dev/
```

#### GITHUB (Repository Link)
Folder name starts with `github`. Links to a GitHub repo.

```
github-1-template-1/
  github.md           # Title + summary
  github.png          # Card image
  githubid            # File containing the GitHub URL
```

The `githubid` file:
```
https://github.com/tutors-sdk/tutors
```

#### ARCHIVE (Downloadable Resource)
Folder name starts with `archive`. Provides a zip download.

```
archive/
  archive.md          # Title + summary
  archive.png         # Card image
  archive.zip         # The downloadable file
```

#### TUTORIAL
Folder name starts with `tutorial`. Simple tutorial content with optional PDF.

```
tutorial-1/
  problem-sheet-1.md  # Title + content
  problem-sheet-1.pdf # Optional PDF
  problem-sheet-1.png # Card image
```

#### PODCAST
Folder name starts with `podcast`. Embeds a podcast episode.

```
podcast/
  podcast.md          # Title + description
  episode             # Service identifier file
```

The `episode` file format:
```
spotify=3cqFe6wRbaadmPosSwckXh
```

---

### 4. FULL EXAMPLE -- HIERARCHICAL COURSE LAYOUT

```
my-course/
  course.md                              # Course title + description
  course.png                             # Course card image
  properties.yaml                        # Course configuration
  calendar.yaml                          # Optional calendar
  
  topic-01-introduction/
    topic.md                             # "# Introduction\nOverview of..."
    topic.png                            # Topic card image
    unit-1/
      main-lesson.md                     # "Main Lesson" (unit title)
      talk-1-welcome/
        welcome.md                       # "Welcome\nOpening remarks"
        welcome.pdf
        welcome.png
      talk-2-overview/
        overview.md
        overview.pdf
        overview.png
      book-a/
        00.Lab-01.md                     # "# Objectives\nGetting started..."
        01.Setup.md
        02.First-Steps.md
        03.Exercises.md
        img/
          main.png                       # Lab card image
          01.png
        archives/
          archive.zip
    unit-2/
      resources.md                       # "Supporting Resources"
      note-1/
        note.md
        note.png
        img/
          01.png
      web-1/
        web.md                           # "Useful Links\nRelevant sites"
        web.png
        weburl                           # "https://example.com"
      archive/
        archive.md
        archive.png
        archive.zip

  topic-02-advanced/
    topic.md
    topic.png
    panelvideo-1/                        # Panel-level video
      video.md
      videoid                            # "dQw4w9WgXcQ"
    panelnote/                           # Panel-level note
      note.md
      note.png
      img/
        01.png
    unit-1/
      lectures.md
      talk-1/
        talk.md
        talk.pdf
        talk.png
    side-unit/                           # Sidebar with labs
      topic-labs.md                      # "# Labs for this Topic"
      book-a/
        00.Lab-02.md
        01.01.md
        02.02.md
        img/
          main.png
```

---

### 5. THE GENERATOR TOOLCHAIN

The course folder is converted to a deployable course by the **tutors CLI**, published to JSR as `@tutors/tutors`. The toolchain is in the `tutors-sdk/tutors-apps` repo under `cli/`.

**Architecture:**

1. **`@tutors/tutors-model-lib`** (JSR package) -- Defines all TypeScript types: `Lo`, `Lab`, `Talk`, `Note`, `Topic`, `Unit`, `Side`, `Course`, `Composite`, etc. Also contains the `decorateCourseTree()` function that enriches the parsed tree with breadcrumbs, panels/units classification, wall indexes, and HTML conversion.

2. **`@tutors/tutors-gen-lib`** (JSR package) -- Contains:
   - `resource-builder.ts` -- `buildTree(dir)`: Recursively walks the filesystem, identifies each folder's LO type by matching folder name against prefixes, and builds a `LearningResource` tree
   - `course-builder.ts` -- `buildCourse(lr)`: Walks the `LearningResource` tree and builds the `Course` object model, reading markdown files, extracting frontmatter, PDFs, images, video IDs, web URLs, etc.
   - `course-emitter.ts` -- Generates static HTML output (for tutors-lite)
   - Template engine (vento templates) for static HTML generation

3. **`@tutors/tutors`** (JSR CLI, v5.0.0) -- The primary generator. Run with:
   ```bash
   deno run -A jsr:@tutors/tutors
   ```
   Outputs `json/tutors.json` -- a single JSON file containing the entire course tree. This JSON is consumed by the **Tutors Reader** (SvelteKit app at `tutors-sdk/tutors`).

4. **`@tutors/tutors-lite`** (JSR CLI) -- A secondary generator producing standalone static HTML:
   ```bash
   deno run -A jsr:@tutors/tutors-lite
   ```
   Outputs to `html/` directory. Deployed via GitHub Pages.

**How the generator determines LO type from folder names:**

The `findLastMatchingString()` function scans path segments from right to left. For each segment, it checks if it starts with any of the known type prefixes: `note`, `archive`, `web`, `github`, `panelnote`, `paneltalk`, `panelvideo`, `podcast`, `talk`, `book`, `lab`, `tutorial`, `unit`, `side`, `topic`, `course`. The first match wins. `book` is immediately aliased to `lab`.

**Deployment options:**
- **Vercel**: Uses `vercel.json` with build command `npx -y deno-bin@latest run -A jsr:@tutors/tutors`. Output is `json/` directory served by the Tutors Reader at `tutors.dev/course/<repo-owner>/<repo-name>`.
- **GitHub Pages** (tutors-lite): Uses the publish-html workflow with `deno run -A jsr:@tutors/tutors-lite`. Outputs static HTML to `html/`.
- **Netlify**: The generator also creates a `netlify.toml` redirect file.

---

### 6. KEY NAMING RULES FOR VALID COURSE SKELETONS

1. **Course root must contain `course.md`** -- the generator checks for this file first and exits if not found.

2. **Folder prefix determines type** -- The folder name must START with the type prefix. Anything after the prefix is a human-readable identifier (e.g., `topic-01-introduction`, `talk-1-welcome`, `book-a`, `unit-2`, `side-extras`).

3. **Each LO folder must contain a `.md` file** -- This provides the title (first line) and summary (second non-blank line). The `.md` filename can be anything.

4. **Image files provide card thumbnails** -- Any `.png`, `.jpg`, `.jpeg`, `.gif`, or `.svg` file in the LO folder becomes its card image. For labs, `img/main.png` is used specifically.

5. **Special marker files**:
   - `weburl` -- Plain text file with URL (for `web` type)
   - `githubid` -- Plain text file with GitHub URL (for `github` type)
   - `videoid` -- Plain text file with YouTube ID or `service=id` (for video-enabled types)
   - `episode` -- Plain text file with `spotify=ID` or `service=ID` (for `podcast` type)

6. **Frontmatter in `.md` files** is optional but supports:
   - `icon.type` and `icon.color` -- Iconify icon override (replaces image)
   - `order` -- Explicit sort order number

7. **Topics appear at course root level** (as direct children). Within topics, content is organized in `unit-*` and/or `side-*` folders, or placed directly (which makes them "standardLos"). Panel types (`panelvideo`, `paneltalk`, `panelnote`) also go directly inside topics.

8. **Lab step files** must follow the `NN.title.md` pattern and are sorted alphabetically. The `00` prefix is conventionally the objectives/intro step.

## Tutors-SDK Course Folder Structure -- Comprehensive Breakdown

### 1. COURSE ROOT FILES (Required)

Every tutors course requires these files at the root:

**`course.md`** (REQUIRED) -- The course title and description. The first line (after optional frontmatter) is treated as the title (leading `#` is stripped). The second non-empty line becomes the summary. The full body is the course's "info" content.

```markdown
# My Course Title

A short description of the course.
```

**`course.png`** (or `.jpg`, `.jpeg`, `.gif`, `.svg`) -- The course card image. This is the visual thumbnail shown in course listings.

**`properties.yaml`** (OPTIONAL but standard) -- Course-level configuration. Key properties:

```yaml
credits: Author name or credits line
slack: https://slack-url
moodle: https://moodle-url
youtube: https://youtube-playlist-url
teams: https://teams-url
zoom: https://zoom-url
parent: course/parent-course-id
auth: 0                    # 0=public, 1+=requires auth
labStepsAutoNumber: false  # auto-number lab steps
llm: 2                     # LLM integration level
ignorepin: 4321            # PIN to reveal hidden topics
portfolio: false           # treat as portfolio of courses
private: 0                 # 1=private course
hideVideos: false
defaultPdfReader: adobe    # or "mozilla"
pdfOrientation: landscape  # or "portrait"
footer: "Footer text"

ignore:                    # list of topic folder IDs to hide
  - topic-10-hidden

companions:                # custom companion links
  piazza:
    link: https://piazza.com/
    title: Piazza Q & A for this course
    icon:
      type: academicons:piazza
      color: info

iconset:                   # custom icon overrides
  moodle:
    type: fa-solid:graduation-cap
    color: warning
```

**`calendar.yaml`** (OPTIONAL) -- Defines a week-by-week calendar overlay.

**`enrollment.yaml`** (OPTIONAL) -- Enrollment/access control data.

**`vercel.json`** (OPTIONAL) -- For Vercel deployment:
```json
{
  "version": 2,
  "buildCommand": "npx -y deno-bin@latest run -A jsr:@tutors/tutors",
  "outputDirectory": "json",
  "framework": null
}
```

---

### 2. LEARNING OBJECT TYPES -- The Complete Taxonomy

The system recognizes learning objects by **folder name prefix**. The `findLastMatchingString` function in `resource-builder.ts` scans each folder path segment from right to left, matching against these prefixes:

**Simple types** (leaf content):
- `note` -- Rich markdown note
- `archive` -- Downloadable zip file link
- `web` -- External web link
- `github` -- GitHub repository link
- `panelnote` -- Note displayed at topic level as a panel card
- `paneltalk` -- Talk displayed at topic level as a panel card
- `panelvideo` -- Video displayed at topic level as a panel card
- `podcast` -- Podcast episode embed
- `talk` -- Presentation/lecture (PDF slides)
- `book` -- (alias for `lab`) Multi-step lab
- `lab` -- Multi-step lab walkthrough
- `tutorial` -- Tutorial with optional PDF

**Composite types** (containers that hold other LOs):
- `unit` -- A named section within a topic (rendered inline)
- `side` -- A sidebar section within a topic (rendered in sidebar)
- `topic` -- A major course section (top-level card on course page)
- `course` -- The root (implicit, not a folder prefix)

**Sort order** when displayed (from `preOrder` map):
course(0), unit(1), side(2), topic(3), talk(4), tutorial(5), book/lab(6/7), note(8), web(9), github(10), archive(11), panelnote(12), paneltalk(13), panelvideo(14), podcast(15)

---

### 3. FOLDER STRUCTURE FOR EACH LEARNING OBJECT TYPE

#### TOPIC
The primary structural unit. Folder name must start with `topic`.

```
topic-01-typical/
  typical.md          # Title (first # line) + summary (second line)
  typical.png         # Card image (any image extension works)
  unit-1/             # Units inside
  unit-2/
```

Or with frontmatter for custom Iconify icon (instead of image):
```
topic-09-svg/
  topic.md            # Can use frontmatter for icon
  topic.png           # OR an image file (icon overrides image)
```

The `.md` file can use YAML frontmatter:
```markdown
---
icon:
  type: emojione:owl
  color: blue
order: 3              # explicit sort order
---
# Topic Title

Summary text here
```

#### UNIT
Groups content within a topic. Folder name starts with `unit`.

```
unit-1/
  main-lesson.md      # Unit title/description
  talk-1-intro/       # Talks inside
  talk-2-explore/
  book-a/             # Labs inside
```

The unit `.md` file is simple -- just the title:
```markdown
Main Lesson
```

#### SIDE (Sidebar Unit)
Like a unit but rendered in a sidebar. Folder name starts with `side`.

```
side-unit/
  topic-labs.md       # Side title
  book-a/             # Labs
  book-b/
  book-c/
```

#### TALK (Presentation/Lecture)
Folder name starts with `talk`. Requires:

```
talk-1-intro/
  introduction.md     # Title (first line) + summary
  introduction.pdf    # The PDF slides (required for rendering)
  introduction.png    # Card image
  videoid             # OPTIONAL: YouTube video ID
```

The `.md` content:
```markdown
Lecture 1

A short summary of the talk, no more than two sentences.
```

The `videoid` file (when present) contains just the YouTube ID:
```
x09E7b2ESE8
```

You can also add `?start=1370&1802` for start/end times.

Frontmatter for custom icons:
```markdown
---
icon:
  type: bi:filetype-pptx
  color: green
---
Hidden Lecture

This lecture should not appear in the wall
```

#### LAB / BOOK (Multi-step Walkthrough)
Folder name starts with `book` (internally mapped to type `lab`). This is the most complex type.

```
book-a/
  00.Lab-01.md        # Step 0 (title step - first # line becomes lab title)
  01.01.md            # Step 1
  02.02.md            # Step 2
  03.03.md            # Step 3
  ...
  07.Exercises.md     # Last step
  img/                # Images referenced in steps
    main.png          # Lab card image (MUST be named "main.xxx")
    01.png
    02.png
  archives/           # Optional downloadable archives
    archive.zip
  videoid             # OPTIONAL: associated video
```

Step naming convention: `NN.title.md` where:
- `NN` is a two-digit sort prefix (00, 01, 02...)
- The text between the first `.` and last `.` becomes the step's `shortTitle`
- The first `# Heading` inside the file becomes the step's full title
- Files are sorted alphabetically, so numeric prefixes control order

The `img/main.png` file is special -- it becomes the lab's card image.

#### NOTE
Folder name starts with `note`. Rich markdown content.

```
note-1/
  note.md             # Full markdown content (title from first # line)
  note.png            # Card image
  img/                # Images used in the note
    01.png
    02.png
  archives/           # Optional downloadable zip
    archive.zip
```

Notes support full markdown: images, code blocks with syntax highlighting, math notation (LaTeX), tables, embedded videos (`::video[src="..."]::`) and podcasts (`::podcast[src="..."]::`)

The `.md` file can have any name, but it must be the ONLY `.md` file in the folder (the system picks the first `.md` file found).

#### PANELNOTE
Identical structure to `note`, but folder starts with `panelnote`. Displayed as a panel card directly on the topic page rather than inside a unit.

```
panelnote/
  note.md
  note.png
  img/
    01.png
```

#### PANELTALK
Identical to `talk` but displayed as a panel card on the topic page.

```
paneltalk/
  talk.md
  talk.pdf
  talk.png
```

#### PANELVIDEO
Video panel displayed at topic level. Requires:

```
panelvideo-1/
  video-main.md       # Title/description
  videoid             # YouTube video ID (just the ID string)
```

The `videoid` file contains the YouTube ID:
```
x09E7b2ESE8
```

For HEAnet/VIMP video services:
```
heanet=MEDIA_ID
```
or
```
vimp=MEDIA_KEY
```

#### WEB (External Link)
Folder name starts with `web`. Links out to a URL.

```
web-1/
  tutors-web-site.md  # Title + summary
  tutors-web-site.png # Card image
  weburl              # File containing the URL (first line)
```

The `weburl` file is a plain text file with the URL on the first line:
```
https://tutors.dev/
```

#### GITHUB (Repository Link)
Folder name starts with `github`. Links to a GitHub repo.

```
github-1-template-1/
  github.md           # Title + summary
  github.png          # Card image
  githubid            # File containing the GitHub URL
```

The `githubid` file:
```
https://github.com/tutors-sdk/tutors
```

#### ARCHIVE (Downloadable Resource)
Folder name starts with `archive`. Provides a zip download.

```
archive/
  archive.md          # Title + summary
  archive.png         # Card image
  archive.zip         # The downloadable file
```

#### TUTORIAL
Folder name starts with `tutorial`. Simple tutorial content with optional PDF.

```
tutorial-1/
  problem-sheet-1.md  # Title + content
  problem-sheet-1.pdf # Optional PDF
  problem-sheet-1.png # Card image
```

#### PODCAST
Folder name starts with `podcast`. Embeds a podcast episode.

```
podcast/
  podcast.md          # Title + description
  episode             # Service identifier file
```

The `episode` file format:
```
spotify=3cqFe6wRbaadmPosSwckXh
```

### 5. THE GENERATOR TOOLCHAIN

The course folder is converted to a deployable course by the **tutors CLI**, published to JSR as `@tutors/tutors`. The toolchain is in the `tutors-sdk/tutors-apps` repo under `cli/`.

**Architecture:**

1. **`@tutors/tutors-model-lib`** (JSR package) -- Defines all TypeScript types: `Lo`, `Lab`, `Talk`, `Note`, `Topic`, `Unit`, `Side`, `Course`, `Composite`, etc. Also contains the `decorateCourseTree()` function that enriches the parsed tree with breadcrumbs, panels/units classification, wall indexes, and HTML conversion.

2. **`@tutors/tutors-gen-lib`** (JSR package) -- Contains:
   - `resource-builder.ts` -- `buildTree(dir)`: Recursively walks the filesystem, identifies each folder's LO type by matching folder name against prefixes, and builds a `LearningResource` tree
   - `course-builder.ts` -- `buildCourse(lr)`: Walks the `LearningResource` tree and builds the `Course` object model, reading markdown files, extracting frontmatter, PDFs, images, video IDs, web URLs, etc.
   - `course-emitter.ts` -- Generates static HTML output (for tutors-lite)
   - Template engine (vento templates) for static HTML generation

3. **`@tutors/tutors`** (JSR CLI, v5.0.0) -- The primary generator. Run with:
   ```bash
   deno run -A jsr:@tutors/tutors
   ```
   Outputs `json/tutors.json` -- a single JSON file containing the entire course tree. This JSON is consumed by the **Tutors Reader** (SvelteKit app at `tutors-sdk/tutors`).

4. **`@tutors/tutors-lite`** (JSR CLI) -- A secondary generator producing standalone static HTML:
   ```bash
   deno run -A jsr:@tutors/tutors-lite
   ```
   Outputs to `html/` directory. Deployed via GitHub Pages.

**How the generator determines LO type from folder names:**

The `findLastMatchingString()` function scans path segments from right to left. For each segment, it checks if it starts with any of the known type prefixes: `note`, `archive`, `web`, `github`, `panelnote`, `paneltalk`, `panelvideo`, `podcast`, `talk`, `book`, `lab`, `tutorial`, `unit`, `side`, `topic`, `course`. The first match wins. `book` is immediately aliased to `lab`.

**Deployment options:**
- **Vercel**: Uses `vercel.json` with build command `npx -y deno-bin@latest run -A jsr:@tutors/tutors`. Output is `json/` directory served by the Tutors Reader at `tutors.dev/course/<repo-owner>/<repo-name>`.
- **GitHub Pages** (tutors-lite): Uses the publish-html workflow with `deno run -A jsr:@tutors/tutors-lite`. Outputs static HTML to `html/`.
- **Netlify**: The generator also creates a `netlify.toml` redirect file.

---

### 6. KEY NAMING RULES FOR VALID COURSE SKELETONS

1. **Course root must contain `course.md`** -- the generator checks for this file first and exits if not found.

2. **Folder prefix determines type** -- The folder name must START with the type prefix. Anything after the prefix is a human-readable identifier (e.g., `topic-01-introduction`, `talk-1-welcome`, `book-a`, `unit-2`, `side-extras`).

3. **Each LO folder must contain a `.md` file** -- This provides the title (first line) and summary (second non-blank line). The `.md` filename can be anything.

4. **Image files provide card thumbnails** -- Any `.png`, `.jpg`, `.jpeg`, `.gif`, or `.svg` file in the LO folder becomes its card image. For labs, `img/main.png` is used specifically.

5. **Special marker files**:
   - `weburl` -- Plain text file with URL (for `web` type)
   - `githubid` -- Plain text file with GitHub URL (for `github` type)
   - `videoid` -- Plain text file with YouTube ID or `service=id` (for video-enabled types)
   - `episode` -- Plain text file with `spotify=ID` or `service=ID` (for `podcast` type)

6. **Frontmatter in `.md` files** is optional but supports:
   - `icon.type` and `icon.color` -- Iconify icon override (replaces image)
   - `order` -- Explicit sort order number

7. **Topics appear at course root level** (as direct children). Within topics, content is organized in `unit-*` and/or `side-*` folders, or placed directly (which makes them "standardLos"). Panel types (`panelvideo`, `paneltalk`, `panelnote`) also go directly inside topics.

8. **Lab step files** must follow the `NN.title.md` pattern and are sorted alphabetically. The `00` prefix is conventionally the objectives/intro step.
